source.title: Identifying Interpretable Visual Features in Artificial and Biological Neural Systems
source.authors: David A. Klindt; S. Sanborn; Francisco Acosta; Frédéric Poitevin; N. Miolane

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether individual neurons are more interpretable or predictable than non-axis-aligned features, and reports that K-Means directions outperform individual neurons on an in-silico psychophysics task. This refines the neuron-level claim but does not test the Qwen3 audit or the language-model-specific versions.
record.gate_note: Figure 5 reports in-silico psychophysics accuracy for neurons and K-Means directions across semantic metrics and task difficulties. The text says directions are more predictable across metrics and difficulties; the plotted values are not stated numerically. Other results about biological recordings do not test the AI-model versions. The paper's claims about the improvement of K-Means over other feature-finding methods are not separately recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares K-Means directions (its own method) with individual neurons in a CIFAR-10 ResNet50 (layer 1) and in brain recordings. It uses an image-similarity interpretability index and in-silico psychophysics. No version is tested as stated. There is no neuron-pole share audit (V1/V2), no language-model scale comparison, and no InceptionV1 cat/car analysis (V3). It gives no interpretable-neuron share across tools or architectures (V4), no attribution graphs (V5), and no simulation scoring on text (V7). For V6, the rows measure directions versus neurons, not whether an activating-example explanation fails to predict where a neuron fires. Neuron accuracy is said to fall at central quantiles, but only in a figure, without numbers, and with a similarity model rather than an explanation. The result is evidence against neurons being the cleanest units, a related construct recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that, in a CIFAR-10 ResNet50 and three visual-cortex datasets, K-Means directions are more interpretable than single units, consistent with superposition. They add that the gap exists even in untrained CNNs, that pairs of neurons can combine into more interpretable directions ('feature synergy'), and that directions transfer better across subjects and sessions.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses visual maximally exciting images, an image-similarity interpretability index, and in-silico psychophysics; it does not use language-model neuron explanations or score simulated activations on text.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that psychophysics accuracy falls as task difficulty increases; the relative advantage of directions is present across low-, mid-, and high-level similarity metrics. It states that the number of clusters K does not impact accuracy in the tested range.

fits_no_version.finding: In ResNet50 layer 1 (CIFAR-10), K-Means directions score higher on the interpretability index and psychophysics accuracy than individual neurons, across color, LPIPS and label metrics. The gap is largest for color and also appears in untrained models and macaque/fMRI data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-axis-aligned directions in vision CNN activation space are more interpretable than individual neurons, contrary to neurons being the cleanest units.

fits_no_version.finding: Neuron psychophysics accuracy falls as query images move from extreme to central activation quantiles (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MEI-based prediction of a vision neuron's firing degrades away from its top activations.

record.problems: The relevant quantitative accuracy values are presented in Figure 5 without numerical values in the text. The study tests one visual model and layer for this comparison, and its psychophysics task is a proxy for interpretability rather than a direct test of whether a written explanation predicts all activations. The authors also note that in-silico psychophysics accuracy is often at ceiling.
record.rows_left_out: None. Biological recording results and other interpretability analyses were not included because they do not test the AI-model version recorded here.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or neuron-pole shares.
No language models, scale range, or dense versus MoE comparison.
Uses a cat/car neuron only as a conceptual illustration (Fig. 1). The InceptionV1 neuron and the pose account are not analysed.
No interpretable-neuron share as a function of tools, architecture or regularization. No InceptionV1-sized estimates.
No attribution graphs or circuits built from neurons.
No natural-language explanation is checked against firing. Psychophysics across activation quantiles is reported only as a figure, using an image-similarity model.
No simulation scoring of explanations on text.

record.verdict_notes: The analysis is restricted to layer 1 because the LPIPS proxy matches human judgments only in early layers (AUC up to 0.71). Authors note psychophysics accuracy is often at ceiling. The reader's V6 'supports' label is removed: the rows compare methods, not explanation failure.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not audit Qwen3-32B or report the proportions of neuron poles with one, two, or unknown jobs.
The paper studies vision systems, not language models, and does not test across model scale, dense versus mixture-of-experts architectures, or trillion-parameter models.
It does not analyze the InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test the pose/recursive-generalization account.
It does not test the stated architecture/regularization explanation or estimate interpretable-neuron shares for InceptionV1-sized models.
It does not evaluate attribution graphs or whether a model's own neurons suffice as circuit units.

Tests predictability from maximally exciting image examples using visual in-silico psychophysics, not explanations written in natural language or predictions on text. It does not report a threshold for when an explanation counts as failing.
It does not simulate neuron activations on new text or report the share of explanations meeting an automated-score threshold.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet50 layer 1 on CIFAR-10; tested image-similarity metrics, task difficulties, and K-Means settings
reader_labels.reason: K-Means directions are reported as more predictable than individual neurons across the tested metrics and task difficulties (r1–r9). This is relative evidence for the stated concern, not a direct demonstration that neuron explanations fail absolutely.
